text.p: Canadian waste and transportation giant Laidlaw Inc. posted a 37 percent jump in fiscal first quarter profits Monday and forecast more profitable growth in 1997.
Laidlaw said net income rose to $68.9 million in the first quarter ended Nov. 30, up from $50.2 million in the same period a year earlier.
Chief Executive Officer James Bullock said in a statement the first quarter results were "a fine start for fiscal 1997."
He said continued strength in transportation and recent deals worth over $2 billion "should all contribute to another year of profitable growth."
Last week, Laidlaw announced plans to acquire American Medical Response Inc. -- the largest healthcare transportation company in the United States -- for $1.12 billion.
Laidlaw also unveiled plans to merge its Environmental Services unit with Delaware-based Rollins Environmental Services Inc. into a new publicly traded company.
Chief Financial Officer Les Haworth said American Medical will begin to add to Laidlaw's earnings in the third quarter of 1997. The Rollins deal is expected to contribute in the fourth quarter.
"We expect to expand both the top line and the bottom line," Haworth said in a telephone interview. He declined to give a specific forecast.
